elements.element: Customer is not subject to any employee non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly binds both parties, including Customer, not to solicit specified employees.

elements.element: The employee non-solicitation restriction is mutual and applies to both parties on the same terms.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “neither party” will solicit covered employees of the other party.

elements.element: The restriction is limited to personnel directly involved in the services.
elements.evidence: It covers only employees “who is or was directly involved in such services.”

elements.element: The restriction lasts no more than 12 months from the end of each covered person's involvement in the services.
elements.evidence: The restriction applies during “twelve (12) months after the end of that person's involvement” in the services.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: The definition of “Solicit” expressly excludes “generally advertising job openings” and follow-up to respondents.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches by individuals are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: The definition excludes activities constituting follow-up to individuals who “voluntarily initiate employment inquiries.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring covered personnel.
elements.evidence: The operative restriction prohibits solicitation to leave employment but contains no independent prohibition on hiring.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because Customer remains bound by a non-solicit. It fully achieves the fallback: the restriction is mutual, limited to directly involved personnel, runs for a single 12-month post-involvement period, retains the required exceptions, and does not create a no-hire restriction. The changes are confined to the non-solicit’s parties, scope, and duration.
